newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS TUMBLE BUT NIKKEI ENDS ABOVE 20,000.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS TUMBLE BUT NIKKEI ENDS ABOVE 20,000.

text.p: Tokyo stocks fell sharply in thin trade on Wednesday but the benchmark Nikkei average finished above the 20,000 level.
Brokers said the fall was triggered by speculative futures sales, adding that the feeble sentiment may linger for a while.
The Nikkei 225 average ended down 320.43 points or 1.57 percent at 20,093.03, the day's low. Its March futures fell 290 points to 20,120.
"Trading volume has been thin all day and it made stock prices volatile," said Masayuki Matsumoto, analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
The Nikkei's closing was marginally below the close at 20,107.11 on September 2, making it the lowest closing price since March this year.

The Nikkei average retained modest losses for most of the day, but the fall accelerated in late afternoon. Brokers said the fragile downside may suggest that the market may continue its corrective phase for a while.
Turnover was light at about 343 million shares, compared with 341 million shares on Tuesday.
Losers overwhelmed gainers 873 to 221, while 165 issues were unchanged.
